name: Classics (Min)

rules.name: Classics Minor Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Students may choose among four fields of study for the minor in Classics: Classical Languages, Ancient History, Literature and Philosophy, and Classical Studies. These fields of study are not declared in Axess or printed on the transcript or diploma.
Students can review the department website for information on how to declare the minor.

children.name: Classical Languages
children.desc: Students must take a minimum of five courses in Greek or Latin. In addition to the five required courses, students must take CLASSICS 150 Majors Seminar (WIM). Choose from the following courses:

children.name: Ancient History
children.desc: Students are required to take a minimum of five courses in history, art history, and archaeology. Courses taken outside of the department may be substituted for one or more of these courses with prior, written approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies. In addition to the five required courses, students must take CLASSICS 150 Majors Seminar (WIM). Courses offered in Latin and Greek that focus on historical topics or authors may count toward this minor with prior approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Choose from the following courses:

children.name: Philosophy and Literature
children.desc: Students must take at least five courses in classical literature or philosophy, including classical science. Courses taken outside the department (for instance, from the Philosophy department) may be substituted for one or more of these courses with prior written approval from the Director of Undergraduate Studies. In addition to the five required courses, students must take CLASSICS 150 Majors Seminar (WIM). Courses in Latin and Greek that focus on philosophical or literary topics or authors may count toward the minor. Choose from the following courses:

children.name: Classical Studies
children.desc: Students must take at least five courses in Classics (any course with subject code CLASSICS) plus CLASSICS 150 Majors Seminar (WIM).

children.name: Classical Studies Electives
children.desc: Students are required to take at least five courses in Classics (any course with subject code CLASSICS)

transferPolicy: University credit earned by placement tests or advanced placement work in secondary school is not counted toward any minor requirement in the department. Work done at other universities or colleges is subject to department evaluation and the university’s transfer credit process.
otherRequirements: A letter grade is required for all courses taken for the minor. No course receiving a grade lower than ‘C’ is counted toward fulfilling minor requirements.
reviewNotes: Choose one of the four fields of study. Each asks for CLASSICS 150, the Majors Seminar, plus five courses from that field's list (any five CLASSICS courses for Classical Studies). Every course must be letter graded with a C or better. Outside courses and Latin or Greek courses on related topics count only with the Director of Undergraduate Studies' approval, so you move those in by hand.
